review_candidates.title: Senior Product Management / Program Mgr Startup
review_candidates.description: About the job MissFit Coaching · Remote (Global) · HQ in Chicago USA - Global Team - Contract - Full-time Reports to: Founder & CEO · Direct reports: None — this role operates through influence and documentation, not managerial authority. Compensation: This is a contract role, fully remote, salary is $1,200 USD with bonus upside based on performance. Fluent English required. Collaborate, in English, with others from the USA, California, Abuja, Lagos Nigeria, Pakestan, and Phillipines. We are a global, collaborative team of 20. And growing fast, About MissFit CoachingMissFit Coaching is an executive career-coaching and reverse-recruiting practice — in plain terms, we help executives run their job search like a business — serving mid-career, white-collar professionals in job transition. We run a fast-moving, distributed team and hold ourselves to the same standard of precision and follow-through we ask our clients to bring to their own job search. This is not a hands-on delivery role — our Client Services team handles client work directly, and our development partners write the code. What this role owns is the operating rhythm and the product itself: plans get built, work gets tracked, status gets reported honestly and on time, the roadmap reflects what the business and its users actually need next, and nothing depends on someone chasing it down. Be clear-eyed about what makes this role hard: you will be accountable for other people's deliverables — engineering output, client-services follow-through, a peer's task list — without having formal authority to manage them. You will hold named colleagues to a standard through relationship, documentation, and persistence, not through org-chart power. On the product side, you will be the single owner of the relationship and roadmap across both of our technical partners — our external development team and our AI automation partner — which means reconciling two different workstreams into one coherent product direction instead of just relaying requests to whichever one is easiest to reach. This is the hardest part of the job, and it is the part we are hiring for most deliberately. If "governance without authority" sounds abstract, picture this: a colleague tells you something is done, and it's your job to verify that before you report it upward — even when that's uncomfortable. You'll be the single point of accountability for whether the business has a clear, current, and truthful picture of what's happening across the team every week — and for whether the platform we run our business on is actually getting better, not just getting built. One more thing, stated plainly: you will not be chased. You are the chaser. No one — including the Founder & CEO — should ever need to follow up with you to find out where something stands. If a report is late, a blocker is stuck, or a colleague has gone quiet, you surface it before anyone has to ask. That direction only runs one way in this role. Our engineering team is awesome - they're ex-amazon developers, and have a fast turnaround. We have been partnering together for two years, and they understand our business well. Operations & Governance Cross-functional governance across Engineering, Client Services, and Operations — keeping all three coordinated against one shared plan. The 90-Day Working Plan ("30-60-90") — building it, keeping it current, and reporting against it every week. ClickUp as the single system of record for all non-client-delivery work: loading approved action items, assigning owners and due dates, and keeping the board accurate and current. Weekly leadership reporting — consolidating status across every department into one clear, specific report, delivered on schedule without being asked. Rollout and adoption of operating standards (for example, our daily commit/close tracking system for Client Services) — not just announcing a new standard, but staying with it until the whole team is actually using it. Proactive status reporting on any major initiative you're driving — leadership should never have to ask where something stands. Product Management for the MissFit Platform Roadmap and prioritization — deciding, with the Founder & CEO, what gets built next by weighing client and Client Services feedback against engineering capacity and business priority. You own the sequencing, not just the task list. The user feedback loop — systematically collecting input from clients and the internal team actually using the platform, and turning it into prioritized, well-defined requirements instead of ad hoc requests. Feature specs and QA ownership — writing complete requirements documents (PRDs), and verifying shipped features actually work as intended, with real users, before they reach clients or staff. Shipped is not the same as done; done means verified. Product metrics — defining and tracking how the platform is actually performing: feature adoption, staff usage rates, client engagement, and any measure that tells you whether the product is improving the business, not just accumulating features. Single ownership of both technical relationships — you are the one person who owns the roadmap and requirements conversation across our external development team and our AI automation partner, reconciling their work into one coherent product direction. What We're Looking For Proven experience in operations, project management, or program management — ideally in a small, fast-moving company where you owned process across multiple functions at once. A track record of building and running structured reporting cadences (weekly reports, project trackers, status dashboards) that leadership actually relies on. Comfort working directly with a founder/CEO and communicating in specific, factual, no-filler language — we value clarity over polish. Direct experience owning a product roadmap and writing requirements documents for a software product, even a small or internal one — you don't need to write code, but you need to have made real build-vs-defer decisions and lived with the results. Experience running a user feedback loop — turning scattered input from end users into prioritized, specific requirements, not just a backlog of requests. Experience managing multiple technical or development partners at once, reconciling their work into a single coherent direction rather than treating each as a separate, disconnected workstream. Strong written communication in English, since most of our coordination happens asynchronously in writing (email, Slack, shared documents). Self-directed follow-through — you flag blockers before you're asked, and you don't wait for a reminder to deliver something you already committed to. A demonstrated habit of verifying status before reporting it — you check that a task is actually done before you tell leadership it's done, even when the person who told you otherwise is a colleague you like and trust. Comfortable holding peers and vendors accountable to deadlines without having formal authority over them. Work Style and LogisticsLocation: Fully remote. Open to candidates in any country. Schedule: We generally align to USA hours - 7 a.m. or so to about 4 p.m. or so. Check what that means in your local time zone before applying — for many non-U.S. time zones this falls in the evening or very early morning, and we want you to make that call with full information rather than discover it after an offer. Direct reports: None. This role has no one reporting into it. Your impact comes entirely through influence, documentation, and follow-through — not through managing people. However, admin and other support is available. Tools: Google Workspace, Slack, ClickUp, WhatsApp, Claude, Perplexity, and our internal client-delivery platform. Training provided on our specific systems; prior experience with similar tools (Asana, Monday.com, Notion, Trello) is a strong substitute. Communication standard: Written updates are specific, dated, and attributed to a named owner. We don't use vague status language like "on track" or "in progress" — every report says what was done, by whom, with a result attached. HOW TO APPLY - Send a video, a brief one, your resume, anything else we should know to Dee@MissFitCoaching.com, subject is "SUCCESS". We move fast.

review_candidates.description: We help the world run better At SAP, we keep it simple: you bring your best to us, and we'll bring out the best in you. We're builders touching over 20 industries and 80% of global commerce, and we need your unique talents to help shape what's next. The work is challenging – but it matters. You'll find a place where you can be yourself, prioritize your wellbeing, and truly belong. What's in it for you? Constant learning, skill growth, great benefits, and a team that wants you to grow and succeed. The SAP Academy for Customer Success is a global development program designed for talent who are early in their career. This is a full time employment based in Cairo, hybrid work model. Who You’ll Become The Account Executive's primary responsibilities include prospecting, qualifying, selling, and closing new business to existing and net new customers. The Account Executive empowers our customers to achieve their full potential by understanding their strategy, unique business goals, and desired outcomes, thereby driving cloud revenue growth through leading dedicated sales efforts to help customers solve their business challenges by positioning value through our solutions. What You’ll Do As an Account Executive within the SAP Next Gen - Academy for Customer Success, you will be responsible for the following: Successfully complete a 10-month learn-apply program, which includes classroom phases and field phases with your sales team, that enhances your support in the role and is a critical customer-facing function within our Customer Success Board Area. Immerse yourself in multi-dimensional, experiential learning focusing on digital transformation, global intelligence, human skills, business and technology acumen, solution/industry knowledge, and strategy/tools/process. Learn how to drive value across the customer lifecycle through solution adoption and ongoing renewals that foster account expansion. Receive onboarding in your local market with on-the-job training and mentoring by a Senior Account Executive in the field. You will be able to work both behind the scenes and directly with customers. The program will enrich your knowledge of SAP and the Customer Success board area and give you professional experience so that you can be ready to serve our customers. We offer full-time employment from day one with practical learning applications for your role. Upon successful completion of the program, you will move into a direct customer-facing sales role in your market and continue to receive mentoring and coaching support to accelerate your growth. Sales roles in scope: Account Executive (AE), Solution Sales Executive (SSE) SSE Focus Areas SAP Business Transformation Management (BTM) - Knowledge in Business Process Management/Business Process Automation applications. SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) & SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) - Knowledge in database and data management, analytics, application development and integration, intelligent technologies, and AI. Understanding of Integration, Application, Data, Infrastructure, and Security technology domains. What You Bring 2–3 years of professional experience in a quota-carrying sales environment in a technology company OR in a role with significant exposure to business processes. Experience generating opportunities, qualifying leads, and managing sales pipelines across a defined territory with a proven track record of building customer relationships and articulating value propositions. A cooperative and productive approach to working relationships, internally and externally. A strong ability to quickly learn new concepts, adapt to changing environments, and apply knowledge to deliver results. An understanding of AI fundamentals, uses, and ethics, to identify business problems solvable with AI. Strong Business Acumen, including demonstrated knowledge of business processes and/or industries. Proficiency in English and Italian to engage with our global and local network. AI focus areas: (AI Adoption Mindset, Agentic AI Day-to Day Practice, and Context Engineering) A curious and agile mindset, with a passion for learning and the resilience to adapt in a fast-paced, evolving environment. Strong problem-solving, project management, and creative thinking skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and communicate ideas clearly and effectively. Emotional intelligence and cultural awareness that support inclusive teamwork and thoughtful stakeholder engagement. A growing foundation in business acumen and emerging technologies—especially artificial intelligence—paired with a results-oriented approach and the courage to take initiative. The SAP Academy for Customer Success is a global development program designed for talent who are early in their career. About SAP Academy For Customer Success The SAP Academy for Customer Success offers a three-year journey that drives accountability and enhances productivity. It enables graduates to make a quick impact in customer-facing roles while fostering career longevity and leadership potential. Join us for a unique opportunity to build a global network, collaborate with customers to solve real business challenges, and gain hands-on experience with world-class cloud solutions — all while learning in a dynamic environment and earning competitive pay and benefits. #SAPAcademyforCustomerSuccess #SAPNextGen SAP Next Gen is our global experience for students and early talent (0–3 years of professional work experience). Being a part of the Next Gen community provides access to a supportive global network, tailored development opportunities, and the ability to contribute to high-impact projects across the business. SAP’s employees across different regions are enabled to do their best job with the right mix of office and remote work according to country-specific guidelines and regulations. In general, our hybrid work setup consists of three days a week in the office or on-site with customers or partners. We are planning a practical and immersive portion of our program, which will likely involve participants spending four (4) weeks, spread across two trips, in San Ramon, California. This experience is designed to provide unparalleled hands-on learning and networking opportunities. During intensive phases of the program, it is critical that all participants are fully engaged and present to ensure maximum learning and success. As such, vacation will not be approved during some critical times of the program. Bring out your best SAP innovations help more than four hundred thousand customers worldwide work together more efficiently and use business insight more effectively. Originally known for leadership in enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, SAP has evolved to become a market leader in end-to-end business application software and related services for database, analytics, intelligent technologies, and experience management. As a cloud company with two hundred million users and more than one hundred thousand employees worldwide, we are purpose-driven and future-focused, with a highly collaborative team ethic and commitment to personal development. Whether connecting global industries, people, or platforms, we help ensure every challenge gets the solution it deserves. At SAP, you can bring out your best. We ultimately believe in unleashing all talent and creating a better world. AI Usage in the Recruitment Process For information on the responsible use of AI in our recruitment process, please refer to our Guidelines for Ethical Usage of AI in the Recruiting Process. Please note that any violation of these guidelines may result in disqualification from the hiring process. ClickUp as the single system of record for all non-client-delivery work: loading approved action items, assigning owners and due dates, and keeping the board accurate and current. Weekly leadership reporting — consolidating status across every department into one clear, specific report, delivered on schedule without being asked. Rollout and adoption of operating standards (for example, our daily commit/close tracking system for Client Services) — not just announcing a new standard, but staying with it until the whole team is actually using it. Proactive status reporting on any major initiative you're driving — leadership should never have to ask where something stands. Product Management for the MissFit Platform Roadmap and prioritization — deciding, with the Founder & CEO, what gets built next by weighing client and Client Services feedback against engineering capacity and business priority. You own the sequencing, not just the task list. The user feedback loop — systematically collecting input from clients and the internal team actually using the platform, and turning it into prioritized, well-defined requirements instead of ad hoc requests. Feature specs and QA ownership — writing complete requirements documents (PRDs), and verifying shipped features actually work as intended, with real users, before they reach clients or staff. Shipped is not the same as done; done means verified. Product metrics — defining and tracking how the platform is actually performing: feature adoption, staff usage rates, client engagement, and any measure that tells you whether the product is improving the business, not just accumulating features. Single ownership of both technical relationships — you are the one person who owns the roadmap and requirements conversation across our external development team and our AI automation partner, reconciling their work into one coherent product direction. What We're Looking For Proven experience in operations, project management, or program management — ideally in a small, fast-moving company where you owned process across multiple functions at once. A track record of building and running structured reporting cadences (weekly reports, project trackers, status dashboards) that leadership actually relies on. Comfort working directly with a founder/CEO and communicating in specific, factual, no-filler language — we value clarity over polish. Direct experience owning a product roadmap and writing requirements documents for a software product, even a small or internal one — you don't need to write code, but you need to have made real build-vs-defer decisions and lived with the results. Experience running a user feedback loop — turning scattered input from end users into prioritized, specific requirements, not just a backlog of requests. Experience managing multiple technical or development partners at once, reconciling their work into a single coherent direction rather than treating each as a separate, disconnected workstream. Strong written communication in English, since most of our coordination happens asynchronously in writing (email, Slack, shared documents). Self-directed follow-through — you flag blockers before you're asked, and you don't wait for a reminder to deliver something you already committed to. A demonstrated habit of verifying status before reporting it — you check that a task is actually done before you tell leadership it's done, even when the person who told you otherwise is a colleague you like and trust. Comfortable holding peers and vendors accountable to deadlines without having formal authority over them. Work Style and LogisticsLocation: Fully remote. Open to candidates in any country. Schedule: We generally align to USA hours - 7 a.m. or so to about 4 p.m. or so. Check what that means in your local time zone before applying — for many non-U.S. time zones this falls in the evening or very early morning, and we want you to make that call with full information rather than discover it after an offer. Direct reports: None. This role has no one reporting into it. Your impact comes entirely through influence, documentation, and follow-through — not through managing people. However, admin and other support is available. Tools: Google Workspace, Slack, ClickUp, WhatsApp, Claude, Perplexity, and our internal client-delivery platform. Training provided on our specific systems; prior experience with similar tools (Asana, Monday.com, Notion, Trello) is a strong substitute. Communication standard: Written updates are specific, dated, and attributed to a named owner. We don't use vague status language like "on track" or "in progress" — every report says what was done, by whom, with a result attached. HOW TO APPLY - Send a video, a brief one, your resume, anything else we should know to Dee@MissFitCoaching.com, subject is "SUCCESS". We move fast.
